content.value_statement: Java teams need clear guidance for real-time voice conversations with Azure AI. This skill supplies VoiceLive setup, authentication, session, audio, event, and voice configuration examples.
actual_capabilities: Shows Maven dependency setup for azure-ai-voicelive.
Explains endpoint and API key environment variables.
Demonstrates API key and DefaultAzureCredential authentication patterns.
Outlines session startup, session options, and event handling.
Covers PCM16 audio requirements, turn detection, and voice selection.
Includes examples for function calling and reactive error handling.
limitations: It is documentation only and does not install the Java package.
It does not validate Azure resource names, keys, or deployment availability.
It does not provide a complete audio capture or playback application.
It references beta SDK APIs that may change.

use_cases.title: Prototype a Java Voice Assistant
use_cases.description: Use Maven setup, authentication, session startup, and audio requirements to plan a VoiceLive proof of concept.

use_cases.title: Plan Azure Authentication
use_cases.description: Compare API key and managed identity approaches before choosing a production credential strategy.

use_cases.title: Tune Conversation Behavior
use_cases.description: Review turn detection, transcription, voices, and interruption behavior for a real-time assistant experience.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up VoiceLive Java
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the azure-ai-voicelive-java skill to show the Maven dependency, required environment variables, and minimal client setup.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Authentication
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare API key authentication and DefaultAzureCredential for an Azure AI VoiceLive Java service. Recommend one for my deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Streaming Session
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Java implementation plan for a real-time VoiceLive session with PCM16 audio, turn detection, transcription, and event handling.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Java VoiceLive design for security, reconnection behavior, session cleanup, and function calling risks. List concrete changes.

output_examples.input: Set up a Java client for VoiceLive.
output_examples.output: A setup checklist with the Maven dependency, endpoint variable, credential choice, and async client initialization steps.

output_examples.input: Help tune turn detection for a hands-free assistant.
output_examples.output: A configuration review covering threshold, prefix padding, silence duration, interruption handling, and audio transcription tradeoffs.
A sequence overview for session creation, speech start and stop events, response audio streaming, completion, and error handling.

best_practices: Prefer DefaultAzureCredential for production deployments when managed identity is available.
Keep VoiceLive keys in environment variables or secret stores, not source files.
Close sessions and handle stream errors so audio connections do not hang.
anti_patterns: Hardcoding Azure endpoints, API keys, or deployment names in shared code.
Skipping audio format checks before sending microphone data to the service.
Treating sample snippets as a complete production voice application.

faq.question: Does this skill run Azure VoiceLive calls?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples for Java code that can call Azure AI VoiceLive.

faq.question: Which Java package does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers the com.azure:azure-ai-voicelive package shown in the skill documentation.

faq.question: Can I use managed identity?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes DefaultAzureCredential as the recommended authentication path.

faq.question: What audio format is expected?
faq.answer: The examples use 24 kHz, 16-bit signed PCM, mono audio.

faq.question: Does it include full microphone capture code?
faq.answer: No. It assumes your application supplies valid PCM16 audio chunks.

faq.question: Is it compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata marks it as supported by Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
